identity.fantasy: A living siege beetle that turns incoming blows into Rage, armor states, regeneration, poison pressure, and violent counterattacks.
identity.one_line: An exoskeleton tank built on Carapace regeneration, Chitin, poison retaliation, Impale, Expulsion, and Molt. It combines high self-repair with AoE poison threat. Recent community builds and discussion consistently identify it as one of the strongest-feeling current dungeon tanks, but that is observational rather than a verified ranking.

mechanics.core_loop: Let incoming attacks build Exposed Flesh, decide whether to clear those stacks through Expulsion, Regrow Exoskeleton, or another effect, maintain a safe amount of Carapace Regeneration, spread Venomtip Poison, and use Impale or kiting to control large packs.

modes.structural_description: Level 20 PassiveIncreases all primary attributes by 15% while in Beetle Form.In addition, increases your hit rating by 3% of all primary attributes.

modes.name: Natural Weapons
modes.structural_description: Increases the critical strike chance of all Beetle Form abilities by 10%.

modes.name: Reformed
modes.structural_description: Level 30 PassiveClearing Exposed Flesh stacks inside Beetle Form now restores health based on stacks cleared.

modes.name: Spider Lord
modes.structural_description: Augments Beetle Form into a Spider Lord, reducing damage taken by -5%, and while Locust Swarm is active your summons now gain 30% increased haste and damage.Casting Hivebreak now has a 40% chance, and melee auto attacks now have a 5% chance, to summon 1 Scarab to aid you in combat for 12 seconds.

mechanics.single_target: Cycle Exposed Flesh into mitigation or poison pressure, keep survival layers active, and use Barbed Stinger and later sustain effects on durable targets.
mechanics.aoe: Expulsion, Venomtip Poison, Impale, Toxic Expulsion, and Locust Swarm create strong area pressure that scales naturally with being attacked by many enemies.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Most survival state lives on the tank rather than one target; Impale lines, pack grouping, kiting, and Molt movement still require spatial control.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Carapace Regeneration, Regrow Exoskeleton, Reformed, Charm of Warding, Locust Swarm, and later regeneration talents create extensive self-sustain; Impale adds a long line stun.
mechanics.group_utility: Fortitude contributes grouping stability, attack-speed reduction, a line stun, and the ability to survive unusually large pulls while damage-over-time effects work.

failure_modes.text: Holding too many Exposed Flesh stacks or using all Carapace Regeneration charges carelessly can turn the spec's survival engine against itself.

Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: most survival state lives on the tank rather than one target; impale lines, pack grouping, kiting, and molt movement still require spatial control.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: carapace regeneration, regrow exoskeleton, reformed, charm of warding, locust swarm, and later regeneration talents create extensive self-sustain; impale adds a long line stun.

enjoy_if.text: You like tanks whose defense, healing, and AoE damage all emerge from reacting to incoming hits.

You enjoy the spec's core cadence: let incoming attacks build exposed flesh, decide whether to clear those stacks through expulsion, regrow exoskeleton, or another effect, maintain a safe amount of carapace regeneration, spread venomtip poison, and use impale or kiting to control large packs.

avoid_if.text: You dislike tracking defensive stacks or making frequent tradeoffs between offense and survival.
You dislike the positioning or swap constraint that most survival state lives on the tank rather than one target; impale lines, pack grouping, kiting, and molt movement still require spatial control.

praise.theme: Recent players consistently praise Fortitude's durability, self-healing, and AoE damage for solo play and large pulls.

frustrations.theme: Guidance warns against blindly maximizing Carapace Regeneration and emphasizes clearing Exposed Flesh correctly.

contested.theme: Current stat advice favors Stamina but mixes Agility, Intellect, armor, and author uncertainty; it is not a verified weight order.

claims.text: A July player guide describes Fortitude as a high-self-healing, physical-damage-resistant AoE DoT tank; it recommends maintaining only one or two Carapace Regeneration stacks, clearing Exposed Flesh deliberately, using taunt for venom interactions, and lining packs for Impale.
claims.notes: Detailed single-author guide from the early-release environment.

claims.text: Several July tank players describe Fortitude as exceptionally durable with strong AoE damage in open-world and dungeon-style pulls.
claims.notes: Levels, gear, and pull sizes are not normalized.

claims.text: Fortitude's central skill test is deciding when Exposed Flesh should be converted into damage, mitigation, healing, or control rather than simply clearing it on cooldown.
claims.notes: Exact encounter thresholds remain situational.
